_comment: Thresholds for python -m evals.run --check, which CI runs on every push.
Each key is a dotted path into the metrics part of evals/results/latest.json; a rate uses its rate value.

Floors are the measured default-run value on the development set minus 0.02, rounded down to two decimals. v0.5 was built by reading that set's failures, so these floors guard against regressions; they don't say how the app does on new data. On the small sets (8 jobs, 40 held-out cases) one or two more errors cross a floor; on the 528 pooled pair labels it takes about ten.

Ceilings are set to the measured value with no margin: the held-out fact checker false-pass rate (the hard rule), the development false-pass rate and the false proven rate of pair statuses may not rise at all.

Measured on pipeline 1.0.0-exact. The v1.0 reading fixes (company suffixes, "Client:" lines, employment terms, intro sentences) left every development-set number where it was, so those floors are unchanged. The document quality floors are new in v1.0, at the measured 1.0 minus 0.02. After a change that moves a number on purpose, rerun the evaluation and update the value here in the same commit.
